newsitem.title: USA: LTV chair sees strong demand for products.
newsitem.headline: LTV chair sees strong demand for products.

text.p: David Hoag, chairman and chief executive officer of LTV Corp, said Friday the steelmaker expects continuing strong demand for its products similar to 1996, despite current rising level of imports.

Hoag made the comment as the company reported a fourth quarter 1996 net income of $34.5 million down slightly from $34.8 million in the comparable 1995 period. Net income per share in both quarters was $0.32.

Hoag said that while LTV seeks to maintain its currentt high production level, output for 1997 may be affected by a planned major blast furnace repair work at its Indiana Harbor Works in the fourth quarter.
"All efforts will be made to complete this necessary repair efficiently to minimize the outage period," he said.
Hoag also said LTV looks forward to begin production at a technologically advanced facility in joint venture with Trico Steel Co in the first quarter of 1997.
Hoag added that LTV has begun investing in a "direct reduced" iron joint venture in Trinidad and Tobago.
The company said its 1996 net income of $109.2 million, down from $184.8 million in 1995, was due to lower average steel selling prices.

Hoag said LTV's record shipments for 1996, the highest since 1988, helped moderate the effects of weak prices. At the same time record production at LTV's Indiana Harbor Works and Cleveland Works' direct hot charge complex helped reduce costs, he said. In the fourth quarter, LTV said effects of lower shipments and lower average selling prices were partially offset by the improved productivity, a $6.0 million pre-tax benefit and lower interest expense.
